videos.desc:

See you on the next project!

videos.t: Vintage Bertram Metal Lathe - Steel Knurled Bandsaw Thumbscrew
videos.desc:
A replacement for a cap head screw which was very tough to remove and tighten by hand, so a little improvement.  A nice little job for the old lathe and good training on something where dimensions are not important.

This lathe was made in Dundas, Ontario, in the late 1800s or early 1900s, there are no serial #'s that I can see on the machine, so if you know more about these machines, please comment.  I'll have more videos coming out as I work with this machine and make some minor improvements to it to keep it running well.

videos.t: Vintage Bertram Metal Lathe Chuck Key - Hand Forged From Shock Absorber Steel
videos.desc:
This lathe was made in the late 1800s or early 1900s, it needed some new parts to make it fully functional.

This Lathe came with a 4 jaw chuck, but was missing the key.  I've been using a socket extension, but it's time to make something dedicated to the job.

I have already made one for the 3 jaw chuck which works well.

videos.t: Vintage Bertram Metal Lathe - Forged Flat Head Screwdriver
videos.desc:
My lathe needed some maintenance, but I didn't have the right tool for the job.  

This tool combines Forging, Woodworking and Metalworking to make a tool that will last for as long as the lathe will.

videos.t: Stanley - Complete Hand Plane Restoration - From Poor to Perform - With CC
videos.desc: This hand plane was given to me along with a rusty bucket of old tools.  I wanted to take the time to bring it back to a good working condition, better than the original if possible.  This is a 1950s or 1960s plane which looked to have nearly no use judging by the condition of the tote (handle).

videos.t: Prevent DAMAGE to your good files - Copper File Sheath - Useful Tool Storage
videos.desc:
I have been wanting to create some type of simple storage for my files for some time.  Leather was an option, and I do like leather work, but it is time consuming, so I thought I would try something different.  Copper is a soft metal, which works fairly easily with a hammer, why not shape it to suit the files and have it protect them in the drawer.  

I will report back in the comments about any reactions which may occur between the copper and the steel file.

videos.t: How to - Vintage Plumb Hammer Restoration - Handle Fabrication - FROM SCRATCH
videos.desc:
I picked up this hammer which was in rough shape a year ago from the antique shop, the handle had been replaced poorly and didn't last.  I made an attempt at a new handle, which loosened up over time because I neglected to dry the handle properly.  This time, the handle will last, see how I make this handle starting from a log.  

The hammer head eye was tapered in two two directions, so I needed to use a unique wedge pattern to account for this.

videos.t: Hewing Hatchet / Axe Restoration Part 4 - Sharpening The Head & Testing
videos.desc:

Fourth step is to sharpen these hatchets and test them out by the shaving test, the nail test and the on wood test.  

The wood tested is ash, and is fairly dry, so this is a real-world test, not pine or cedar which is soft and very easy to work.

The goal is to produce 2 quality hatchets which are very functiona

This vintage lathe has lots of life left in it and with a few new parts and some TLC, I'm going to get it in tip-top shape.

videos.t: Vintage Bertram Metal Lathe Restoration - Hand Forged Spanner Wrench for Stuck Spindle Bolt Removal
videos.desc:
The spindle end-play bolt has been stuck since I bought the machine, this allows any lateral movement to be taken up and allows for wear also.  The problem is that I could not get any movement out of this bolt because I didn't have the right tools for the job.  In this video I attempt to make a Spanner wrench and if you watch the video, you can see if this was a success or a fail.  

For reference, if you are planning on using steel from clamps, be prepared to forge a tough alloy material, one of the hardest materials I have worked with so far.  

Enjoy and send me some feedback in the comment
